title: Lifting diagonalizable homomorphisms over a complete local base
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] such that $A\to\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and put $k=A/\mathfrak m$ and $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. An $S$-group scheme is a group object in schemes over $S$; homomorphisms respect multiplication, identity and inverse. Let $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$ be an affine $S$-group scheme with $B$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra which is flat as an $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Assume $G_k=G\times_S\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-base-change] is of multiplicative type: on an fppf covering of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pc-fppf-site] it is isomorphic to $D(M')$ for finitely generated abelian groups $M'$. Here $D_A(M)=\operatorname{Spec}A[M]$ has the group-algebra Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. For every finitely generated abelian group $M$, restriction is a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{S\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(D_A(M),G)\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-}\mathrm{gp}}(D_k(M),G_k).$$
If $j_0:D_k(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}G_k$ is an isomorphism, its unique lift $j:D_A(M)\to G$ is an open and closed immersion [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Neither smoothness nor commutativity of $G$ is assumed, and torsion in $M$ is allowed.

source.place: Theorem B.3.2(2), printed pp.288-290, split source, including both the Hom bijection and the open-and-closed-immersion assertion. WANTED locally as literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf; online statement and proof read. No Stacks tag states this structural result.

proof.text: Write $H=D_A(M)$, $A_n=A/\mathfrak m^n$ and $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}A_n$ for $n\geq1$. For any $A$-algebra $R$, the inverse maps $A[M]\otimes_A R\leftrightarrows R[M]$, $e_m\otimes r\leftrightarrow re_m$, identify $H_R$ and its three group operations with $D_R(M)$, by the affine fibre-product formula. Finite generators $m_1,\ldots,m_t$ of $M$ give algebra generators $e_{m_i},e_{-m_i}$ of $A[M]$. The finite-type/Noetherian result makes both this algebra and $B$ finitely presented over $A$. Their quotients over $A_n$ remain finitely presented by reducing generators and relations. Flat module base change makes $B\otimes_A A_n$ flat over $A_n$. The ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^n$ is nilpotent with quotient $k$, so [lem-sfb-nilpotent-flat-multiplicative-deformation] makes $G_n$ of multiplicative type, for every $n$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(2), printed pp.289-290; agent assembly of nilpotent deformation, existing character duality and effectivity, and an affine ideal/translation proof of openness. Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: We verify that reduction $\operatorname{Hom}(H_n,G_n)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_1,G_1)$ is bijective. Choose an fppf cover of $S_n$ diagonalizing $G_n$ and refine it by affine opens. On each such affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the target is $D_R(N)$ and the source is $D_R(M)$. The inverse image $U_1$ is defined by the nilpotent ideal $\mathfrak mR$, so $|U_1|=|U|$: every prime contains that ideal, and the closed subset is the whole spectrum. The character-duality statement [lem-sfb-relative-diagonalizable-character-duality] identifies homomorphisms over $U$ with locally constant character maps $N\to M$; reduction does not change these maps or their underlying open decompositions. Thus any given special-fibre homomorphism lifts uniquely over $U$. On pairwise overlaps the two lifts agree: refine again by affine opens and use the same character-duality argument; the target is already diagonalized by restriction of either trivialization. Uniqueness on these opens gives equality on the overlap by morphism gluing. The cover after pullback to $H_n$ is fppf, hence fpqc. Representable fpqc descent glues the local maps to $H_n\to G_n$. The three homomorphism equations and the prescribed reduction hold after that same covering, hence hold by uniqueness of descent. The same local uniqueness proves uniqueness of the global lift.

proof.text: Given $u_1:H_1\to G_1$, let $u_n$ be its unique lift over $S_n$ from Step 2. Reduction of $u_{n+1}$ to $S_n$ has special fibre $u_1$, so uniqueness in Step 2 makes it equal to $u_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-adic-diagonalizable-hom-effectivity] to this compatible family, using precisely the complete Noetherian local ring $A$, finitely generated $M$, and affine finite-type target $G$ in our hypotheses. It gives a unique $u:H\to G$ reducing to every $u_n$, in particular to the prescribed $u_1$. Conversely any two lifts of $u_1$ have equal reductions at every $n$ by Step 2 and are equal by the injectivity in effectivity. This proves the asserted Hom bijection.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(2), printed pp.289-290; agent assembly of nilpotent deformation, existing character duality and effectivity, and an affine ideal/translation proof of openness. Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Now let $j_0:H_k\xrightarrow{\sim}G_k$ and let $j:H\to G$ be its lift. Define its kernel by $K=H\times_{G,e_G}S$. On rings this is $\operatorname{Spec}(A[M]/I)$, where $I=(j^*(b)-\epsilon_G(b):b\in B)$. It is a closed subgroup of $H$, and $K_k=1_k$ since $j_0$ is an isomorphism, by the fibre-product formula. Choose generators of $M$ to give a surjection $\mathbf Z^t\twoheadrightarrow M$; the resulting surjection $A[\mathbf Z^t]\twoheadrightarrow A[M]$ embeds $H$ as a closed subgroup of the displayed split torus in [lem-sfb-local-torus-subgroup-special-trivial]. Thus the same node applies to $K$ as a closed subgroup of that torus and gives $K=1_S$. The composite coordinate quotient is surjective, so closedness here is the affine quotient criterion, without a flatness assumption on $K$. For any $S$-scheme $T$, $j(h)=j(h')$ implies $h(h')^{-1}\in K(T)=\{1\}$, hence $h=h'$. Thus $j$ is a monomorphism in the required functor-of-points sense.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(2), printed pp.289-290; agent assembly of nilpotent deformation, existing character duality and effectivity, and an affine ideal/translation proof of openness. Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: The source $H=D_A(M)$ is a multiplicative-type group of finite presentation by Step 1, and the target $G$ is affine of finite presentation there. The monomorphism of Step 4 is therefore a closed immersion by [lem-sfb-affine-multiplicative-type-monomorphism-closed]. Write it as $\operatorname{Spec}(B/L)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$ for an ideal $L\subseteq B$. Both $H$ and $G$ are flat over $A$: $A[M]$ is free on its basis, and $B$ is flat by hypothesis; use the flat affine criterion. Apply [lem-sfb-flat-closed-family-ideal-base-change] with $T=S$, $X=G$, $Z=H$. Its exact ideal sequence after base change to $k$ identifies $L/\mathfrak mL$ with the kernel of $B/\mathfrak mB\to (B/L)/\mathfrak m(B/L)$. This map is the coordinate isomorphism of $j_0$, so $L/\mathfrak mL=0$, that is, $L=\mathfrak mL$. The Noetherian finite-type theorem makes $B$ Noetherian, so $L$ is a finite $B$-module.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(2), printed pp.289-290; agent assembly of nilpotent deformation, existing character duality and effectivity, and an affine ideal/translation proof of openness. Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the annihilator form of Nakayama to the finite $B$-module $L$ and the ideal $\mathfrak mB$. It supplies $f\in1+\mathfrak mB$ with $fL=0$. Therefore on the principal open $V=D(f)\subseteq G$ the quotient $B_f\to(B/L)_f$ is an isomorphism: $L_f=0$. This gives a factorization $V\to H\hookrightarrow G$. Moreover $V$ contains the entire identity section: the augmentation $\epsilon_G:B\to A$ sends $f$ to $1+\mathfrak m$, a unit in the local ring $A$ (a nonunit lies in its unique maximal ideal). Thus the identity map $S\to G$ factors through $V$. The principal open and its structure sheaf are exactly $\operatorname{Spec}B_f$ by the basic-open spectrum description.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes, Theorem B.3.2(2), printed pp.289-290; agent assembly of nilpotent deformation, existing character duality and effectivity, and an affine ideal/translation proof of openness. Local archive WANTED.

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-sfb-flat-subgroup-identity-neighbourhood-open] to the closed subgroup $j:H\hookrightarrow G$ and the open $V$ from Step 6. The factorization through $H$ and the identity factorization are supplied there. The source $H\to S$ is flat by Step 5 and locally finitely presented by Step 1. The lemma makes $j$ an open immersion, while Step 5 already made it a closed immersion. This is the required open-and-closed assertion. None of the steps imposed smoothness or commutativity on $G$, or excluded torsion in $M$.
